_README: OPTIONAL hand-maintained provider notes: ToS posture + evidence class, keyed by the provider/wallet name buckets.sh assigns (matched case-insensitively against a bucket's `provider`, then its `local_providers`; first match wins). Never fetched at runtime - edit by hand whenever you learn something, or delete the file, and nothing breaks; `fa show`/`fa lanes -v` just stop printing the TOS line. tos: ok | caution | avoid | unknown. Provenance note (kept here, deliberately never surfaced in `note` below or in any command output - a per-entry `note` is user-facing guidance, not a citation trail): the initial ratings and quota figures were seeded 2026-09-27 from an external free-tier ToS survey of these providers; re-verify before leaning on any of it for anything that matters. A provider absent from this file has simply not been looked at yet, which is not the same as 'ok'.

openrouter.ai.note: External research rates this provider's terms 'caution' for proxy/relay-style use. This is fa's primary lane (kilo/openrouter.ai, see docs/dev/SESSION.md's lane table) - not a reason to stop using it, a reason to have actually read its terms before leaning on it hard.

openrouter.note: same wallet as openrouter.ai under a different local provider name - see that entry.

opencode.note: External research rates proxy/relay-style use of opencode's built-in free gateway 'avoid'. That is exactly the usage pattern of fa's own opencode-provider lane (see SESSION.md's lane table) - not this project's own legal read; verify current terms yourself.

agy.note: same rating as opencode above, per the same external research. Not a lane on this machine yet - worth reading before adding one.

groq.note: ~30M/mo across five per-model caps; no payment method required at signup. Net-new candidate wallet - not yet reachable through any fa adapter without a hermes credential_pool entry or a hand-edited kilo.jsonc provider.

glm-cn.note: Z.AI / Zhipu - one of the better-rated providers here for ToS posture. Uncapped + ~20M signup bonus. Net-new candidate; see 'zhipu'.

zhipu.note: same underlying account as glm-cn/glm (they share one poolKey, zhipu-flash-free) - see glm-cn.

deepseek.note: one-time ~5M, no credit card required, 30-day expiry. Net-new candidate.

mistral.note: ~1B/mo - the single largest pool tracked here - but its own terms scope free use to 'personal needs' only. Net-new candidate.

hyperbolic.note: one-time ~5M via a $1 trial credit. Net-new candidate.

nara.note: ~210M/mo - ToS posture is ambiguous rather than a clean ok/caution/avoid pick. Net-new candidate; read its terms yourself before adding it.

xkiro.note: ~150M/mo shared across 39 models on one daily allowance. Net-new candidate.

llm7.note: ~150M/mo per the figure currently tracked here (a stale, deprecated 4.3M constant exists for this provider elsewhere - if this number is ever re-verified, trust this file over that one). Requires a free token from token.llm7.io. Net-new candidate.

cohere.note: ~800K/mo - its own trial keys are documented as 'not for production'. Net-new candidate.

nvidia.note: uncapped and genuinely keyless, but scoped 'dev/eval only, not production' by its own terms. Net-new candidate, zero signup friction.

stepfun.note: already one of the models on this machine's nous/hermes lane (see docs/dev/SESSION.md's lane table) - not a new wallet, just a terms note on an existing one.
